sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Live-cell imaging (PMC9780758 L3/L4): GFP-tagged CRB2 is robustly detectable at the plasma membrane by live-cell imaging, confirming surface display. Trafficking of GFP-tagged WT CRB2 to the PM is confirmed; disease-associated ECD variants (C629S, R633W, N800K, R1249Q) show altered trafficking relative to WT, demonstrating the construct is functional as a trafficking reporter. Quantitative PM signal is used as a readout for variant pathogenicity.
sites.rationale: L1 and L2 both explicitly state that GFP/SNAP/HaloTag is inserted into the 13th EGF-like repeat of full-length membrane-anchored CRB2 (aa 1–1285) after an aspartate described as position 1095. Python search of the canonical sequence finds no D at 1095 (which is V) but finds D at 1096; the paper's numbering is consistently offset by −1 from canonical UniProt, so the canonical insert_after_residue is 1096. Position 1096 is 129 residues from the TM boundary (1225), well within the extracellular span (29–1224), and the construct is validated by robust live-cell PM imaging and disease-variant trafficking assays (L3, L4, L5, L12). Full-length human CRB2 (aa 1–1285) membrane-anchored construct with GFP, SNAP, or HaloTag inserted within the 13th EGF-like repeat of the extracellular domain. The paper states the tag is 'inserted after an aspartate at position 1095'; the only aspartate in that vicinity is at canonical UniProt position 1096 (the paper's numbering is offset by −1 relative to canonical). Construct expressed in cell lines with a podocyte background and used for live-cell imaging and disease-variant trafficking analysis.

sources.claim: The pENTR plasmids carrying cDNA inserts encoding for codon-optimized or wild-type (wt) human CRB2 wt (amino acids [aa] 1–1285) with GFP-, SNAP-, or HaloTag within the 13th EGF-like repeat of the ECD (inserted after an aspartate at position 1095) have been described earlier ( 14 ).

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-HA immunostaining of 6-day zebrafish rods (L9): HA-tagged Crb2a constructs are detected at the rod cell surface by confocal imaging with anti-HA antibodies, confirming extracellular accessibility of the HA tag in the full-length membrane-anchored context. No functional assay of human CRB2 at this exact junction is reported.
sites.rationale: L7 and L8 report that all seven zebrafish Crb2a full-length constructs carry an HA tag immediately after the signal peptide cleavage site, confirmed at the rod cell surface by anti-HA staining (L9). Zebrafish Crb2a is a close ortholog of human CRB2; the topology is conserved (single-pass type I with a large extracellular domain). For human CRB2, the SP ends at residue 28 (canonical landmarks), so the equivalent junction is insert_after_residue=28 (S|L). This position is topology-derived because no residue number is given for the zebrafish construct and the human junction is inferred from the SP boundary. The position is distinct from the AU1 site at 33/34 (L10), which is 5 residues further into the mature ECD. Zebrafish Crb2a full-length membrane-anchored constructs (expressed in rods under the rod opsin promoter as stable transgenic lines) were engineered with an HA tag (YPYDVPDYA) placed immediately after the signal peptide cleavage site, placing the tag at the extracellular N-terminus. The SP used was from zebrafish Crb2b; the HA tag was engineered 'just after the SP' in all seven Crb2a constructs tested. Surface display was confirmed by anti-HA immunostaining in 6-day zebrafish rods (L9). This is indirect evidence for human CRB2: zebrafish Crb2a is a close ortholog. For human CRB2, the SP ends at residue 28 (canonical), so the equivalent junction is 28/29.

sources.claim: All constructs have an N'terminal signal peptide (SP) taken from zebrafish Crb2b (SignalP 3.0 Server) and an influenza hemagglutinin (HA) tag (YPYDVPDYA) just after the SP.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Co-immunostaining with anti-AU1 and anti-γ-tubulin antibodies in ARPE19 cells (L11): AU1::CRB2 is detected at the cell surface by anti-AU1 immunostaining, confirming extracellular accessibility of the tag. Cells expressing only moderate levels were selected to avoid overexpression artifacts. No functional assay beyond surface detection is reported.
sites.rationale: L10 explicitly names the junction as 'between amino acids 33/34' of full-length human CRB2 in a membrane-anchored construct. Python confirms residue 33 = T and residue 34 = V in the canonical sequence; position 33 is 5 residues into the mature extracellular domain (SP ends at 28), 1192 residues from the TM boundary, with no cysteines within 5 residues of the junction. L11 confirms surface accessibility by anti-AU1 immunostaining in ARPE19 cells. The site is classified terminal_n because it lies very close to the mature N-terminus (5 residues in), functioning as a near-N-terminal extracellular tag. Full-length human CRB2 in a CMV-driven AAV2-ITR construct with a codon-optimized CRB2 cDNA encoding an AU1 epitope tag (DTYRYI) inserted between amino acids 33 and 34. The construct (CMV-AU1::hCRB2-spA) was transiently expressed in ARPE19 cells and detected by co-immunostaining with anti-AU1 antibodies, confirming surface-accessible display of the AU1 epitope in the extracellular domain of the membrane-anchored protein.

sources.claim: CMV-­AU1::h CRB2 -­spA was synthesized at GenScript (USA) and cloned into pUC57, thereafter sub cloned into pUC57-­ ITR. pUC57-­ITR-­CMV-­AU1:: CRB2 -­spA contained the CMV promoter, codon-­optimized CRB2 cDNA encoding a DTYRYI AU1-­tag between amino acids 33/34 of CRB2 , a synthetic poly-­adenylation sequence, flanked 5’ and 3’ by inverted terminal repeats (ITR) of AAV2. pEGFP control vector was from Invitrogen (ThermoFisher Scientific, Courtaboeuf, France).

literature_notes: Three ledger-supported sites identified. L1 and L2 are the primary citations for the GFP/SNAP/HaloTag site at canonical 1096; L3, L4, L5, and L12 provide additional validation of the same construct and are not cited separately. The paper's stated position '1095' is offset by −1 from canonical UniProt numbering (the only aspartate in the vicinity is at canonical 1096); this is documented and the canonical position is used. L6 and L9 provide additional in vivo validation for the zebrafish Crb2a HA-tag site already grounded in L7/L8. Disease-associated point mutations mentioned in L3/L5 (C614, C629S, R633W, N800K, R1249Q) are not tag insertion sites and are not included in other_positions, as the ledger reports them as missense variants affecting trafficking, not as tag-insertion experiments. No intracellular tag insertions or function-abrogating insertions are reported in the ledger for CRB2.
